name: SDC Games
description: A 2-day multi-domain challenge covering AI/ML, Coding, Cyber Security, Web Development, Design, and PR. Day 1 tests multiple independent wings; Day 2 combines finalists into common cross-domain scenario challenges.
rules: Day 1 has 3 technical rounds + 1 non-technical fun round. Participants cannot pick the same technical domain twice on Day 1. Top scorers advance to Day 2.

name: Smash Karts
description: A 2-tier robotics racing tournament: bring your own custom car to compete in a knockout bracket, or enter the learner track to debug microcontroller C++ code, wire sensors, and race with power-ups.
rules: Bracket system for custom cars. Learner track features 3 rounds: Microcontroller code correction, Wiring sensors, and Track race with power-ups.
poc: Krishnanarayanan M (+91 98460 32569), Kallavi Sree Sathya Sivani (+91 7396292887)

name: Impact Tank
description: Structured student startup challenge taking participants from problem identification through prototype building and market validation, culminating in an offline finale at NIT Warangal with a 30K prize pool.
rules: Shortlisted teams demonstrate interactive prototypes at the Impact Expo, followed by a final pitch presentation and Q&A session before an expert jury panel.

name: KBC - Kaun Banega Crorepati
description: A knowledge quiz event modelled on the iconic TV game show. Tests participants' trivia knowledge, quick thinking, and composure under pressure on the Hot Seat.
rules: Round 1: Fastest Fingers First (SMS 5-digit sequence). Round 2: Standard Hot Seat MCQs with 4 lifelines (50:50, Audience Poll, Phone a Friend, Double Dip). Wrong answer eliminates participant at the last safety milestone.

name: MUSIC CORNER
description: Interactive walk-through stations demonstrating motion-sensor Air Guitars (Arduino + MPU6050), electronic synthesizers (555 timer, LDR, LM386), and wearable ESP32 motion-controlled Air Drums.
rules: Open demonstration conducted for experiential hands-on learning and musical entertainment.

name: 60 Seconds: Chemical Apocalypse
description: Hands-on disaster response simulation. Following a plant chemical leak, teams scramble for supplies in 60 seconds, build filtration masks, operate emergency valves, and trade survival resources.
rules: Designated runner enters supply scramble (max 2 items per run). Inventory is locked for subsequent crisis stages, open bartering windows, and credential verification challenges.

name: RUBE WARS
description: Team engineering challenge to design and construct a continuous chain-reaction machine accomplishing a set target using 6 to 9 mechanisms from a catalogue of 15 mechanisms.
rules: Single round, 45-60 min build and test window. Machine must trigger from a single start point and proceed without manual intervention. Evaluated out of 100 marks.

name: SpaceWars
description: Wear physical gauntlet-type gloves with haptic feedback to fly virtual drones, evade alien attacks, and fight opponents in an interactive solo or 1v1 battle arena.
rules: Solo or 1v1 stations. Score awarded based on reaction time, defense, and target eliminations.

name: Edge Olympics
description: EdgeAI-based constrained hardware challenge where participants deploy and optimize deep learning algorithms within tight compute, power, and memory limits on physical embedded boards.
rules: Problem statements distributed at event start. Teams evaluated on accuracy, execution latency, model footprint, and resource optimization.

name: Vehicle Demonstration
description: Showcase powered by 4 student vehicle teams (Team Mechaholics, Team Spardhak, Team Mechxhausters, and Team Ashvaratha) presenting custom quad-bikes, ATVs, Formula race cars, and go-karts.
rules: Touching the vehicles without the permission of the respective team members is strictly prohibited.

name: Saponify and Aroma Lab
description: Two hands-on chemistry workshops running side by side: formulate and mould your own glycerin soap at Saponify, and blend fragrance pyramid notes to craft a 10ml roll-on perfume at Aroma Lab.
rules: Conducted in batches of 25 from 10 AM to 5 PM. Non-competitive hands-on learning. Every participant takes home what they make and receives a certificate.

name: Mech Tag
description: Structured zero-contact 3v3 laser tag tournament inside a custom arena with dynamic scoring, hit deductions, anti-camping protocols, and scattered hidden objects to retrieve under fire.
rules: Fixed obstacles cannot be moved or climbed. Clear line of sight required (no blind firing). 20-30s maximum camping rule per cover spot.

name: DEFCON
description: Live attack-and-defense cybersecurity hackathon where teams fortify their own machines against exploits while scanning, breaking into, and escalating privileges across rival systems.
rules: Round 1 (Fortify) allows patching and configuration only. Round 2 (Attack) opens the arena network for live exploitation. DoS attacks strictly prohibited. Automated scoring tracks foothold and full takeover milestones.

name: Business Frenzy
description: Interactive business strategy simulation: manage a virtual purse, trade smartphone component cards, pivot in response to sudden market news shocks, and pitch your completed product to judges.
rules: Teams receive starting purse and feature cards. Rounds alternate between open trading, technology auctions, and market shocks. Final locked product pitched before judges.
poc: Arushi Pundir (9068944236), Tushar Jain (9864512346), Anurag Sharma (9815880722)

name: Forensic Investigation
description: Step into a staged crime scene: uncover invisible ink messages under UV light, lift latent fingerprints, analyze chromatography evidence, and deliver your verdict before time expires.
rules: 15 minutes inside crime scene room to collect clues followed by 15 minutes in writing room to submit verdict report. No prior forensics background required.

name: Warangal Trading Ring 2.0
description: 5 simulated trading days compressed into a single 90-minute financial simulation. Manage ₹10,00,000 in virtual capital across 15-20 asset classes amid unexpected news releases and market shocks.
rules: Real-time order execution across equities and commodities. Final standings determined by total portfolio valuation and risk-adjusted return.

name: Venture Vortex
description: An All-India Entrepreneurship Competition: teardown a top Indian startup, formulate a go-to-market/MVP execution plan, and pitch live to a boardroom panel at NIT Warangal.
rules: Round 1 (Startup teardown) and Round 2 (Strategy/MVP challenge) conducted online. Finalists present 5-10 min strategy deck with 15 mins Q&A before judges.

name: ECO CITY
description: A sustainability-simulation game where teams use a fixed budget to build a resilient city. Balance renewable energy, agriculture, and housing to survive year-by-year without environmental collapse.
rules: 30-minute build phase using the provided web simulation tool. Deterministic engine scores max survival years (capped at 300 years). Ties broken by lowest peak pollution and lowest total budget spend.

name: MECHATRONICS GALA
description: Flagship multi-event showcase bringing together autonomous F1TENTH racing (Turing Track), human-vs-AI robotic arm gameplay (AI Gambit), and obstacle drone piloting (Mach Sprint).
rules: Turing Track vehicles must run all compute onboard. Mach Sprint drones piloted via Wi-Fi smartphone app. AI Gambit features continuously monitored safety E-stops.

name: Chem-E-Car Showdown
description: Build a small vehicle powered and stopped entirely by chemical reactions—no batteries, motors, mechanical brakes, or electronic timers permitted.
rules: Vehicle fits within 40x30x20 cm. Target distance and payload revealed 1 hour before run. Closest stop to line wins; no manual intervention after release.

name: RoboCannonade
description: Robotics competition where teams build and operate a motorized pan-tilt launcher to accurately hit targets across an arena using a single-shot table tennis ball mechanism.
rules: Stationary robot with min 3 DOF fitting in 50x50x50 cm starting volume. Wireless control or auto-aiming computer vision bonus. External participants bring custom builds; internal NITW teams use identical kits.

name: ∑ o poly
description: Strategy-driven mathematical board game and quantitative competition. Players traverse conceptual milestones across calculus, computing, operators, and topology to build mathematical empires.
rules: Solo participation. Round 1: Online Unstop math/logic quiz. Round 2: Mass digital board game. Round 3: Top 16 finalists battle live on-site at NITW during Technozion.

name: Delta Code
description: Computational and mathematical problem-solving competition challenging teams to solve mathematical models and implement solutions using Python, NumPy, SciPy, SymPy, and Matplotlib.
rules: Round 1: Online math & logic screening on Unstop. Round 2: Solve assigned problem statement in strongest domain using Python followed by online demo presentation.

name: Metamagic
description: Hands-on materials science exhibition where participants observe smart materials, shape memory phenomena, and examine microstructures across interactive discovery stations.
rules: Walk-in interactive demonstration open to all branches and years.

name: Aim for the best
description: A competitive dart challenge combined with technical clue-guessing. Teams throw darts at metal sectors (Steel, Aluminium, Copper, Zinc, Lead) and answer Marvel/DC-themed materials questions.
rules: 5 darts per team. Hits on labelled metal sectors unlock questions; correct answers add score points. Darts landing outside receive no score.

name: Meta Armor
description: Thermal-protection-system design challenge. Teams act as materials engineers to fabricate a lightweight thermal shield for a small re-entry capsule tested under direct flame exposure.
rules: 10 min design & virtual budgeting, 20 min physical construction, standardized heat test rig, followed by failure analysis and redesign.

name: ARCADE
description: Interactive robotics and embedded-systems challenge where teams develop algorithms for AI Air Hockey puck-tracking or Robot Strike multi-target robotic arm tracking.
rules: Write and validate control logic in MATLAB simulation before testing on Raspberry Pi/ESP32 real-time hardware. Evaluated on accuracy, response speed, and stability.

name: the engineering challenge
description: A circuit of 4 to 5 hands-on mixed engineering mini-challenges testing rapid mechanical assembly, spatial coordination, and applied physics.
rules: 4 to 5 fast-paced rounds. Points awarded based on the number and speed of games successfully completed.

name: Neural Core(Mind controlled challenge)
description: Mind-controlled biofeedback demonstration: participants wear an EEG headset and sustain cognitive focus for 10 consecutive seconds to cause a pool of ferrofluid to spike over high-power electromagnets.
rules: Solo interactive challenge with live brainwave frequency telemetry and focus meters displayed on an external monitor.

name: Bid to Build
description: Civil engineering challenge testing strategic resource allocation and construction execution. Bid on materials within a virtual budget and construct a load-bearing prototype.
rules: Round 1: Virtual budget material bidding. Round 2: Timed model construction using only acquired inventory. Models evaluated on strength-to-weight ratio and load capacity.

name: INTO THE VOID
description: VR experience where technology meets thrill, fear, and fun. Participants step into a virtual world filled with unexpected challenges, intense situations, and terrifying surprises, keeping their nerves under control and reacting quickly.
rules: Individual VR run within a fixed time limit. Follow coordinators' instructions. No running, jumping, sudden movements, or misuse of VR equipment. Participants may stop at any time if uncomfortable. Coordinators' decision is final.

name: Jahaaz
description: Flagship nautical event at the central fountain in front of the Main Building. Custom RC boats (ESP32, 380 DC motor, 30A ESC, MG90S servo rudder, 2S LiPo) tackle a speed sprint, an obstacle slalom, and a head-to-head elimination final through active fountain sprays.
rules: 3 participants and 1 RC boat per team. Navigate the water maze through checkpoints, solve puzzles and dynamic QR challenges, collect electronic components, complete the final circuit and decode the Morse-code message. Highest total valid score wins. No interference, external assistance, QR sharing/tampering or unauthorised shortcuts. Follow marshal instructions; only approved equipment allowed.

name: Model Hovercraft Challenge
description: Workshop and competition in one: teams learn hovercraft mechanics, build a working model from a standard kit, then race it through challenge tracks. Teaches air lift, thrust, reduced friction, and steering control.
rules: Engineering or technically skilled college students; each participant joins only one team; register with a team name. Phase 1: hands-on workshop (Oct 25) to build the kit hovercraft. Phase 2 (Oct 31): kit build check (~2 hrs) and testing with mandatory safety check; no parts outside the official kit. Phase 3: Race, Obstacle Course, Water Race, Precision Landing. Phase 4: scores from all 4 tracks plus judges' design and presentation scores; highest total is Hovercraft Champion.

name: Glow Wall
description: Hands-on phosphorescence activity. Use UV light to draw, write, and create patterns on a phosphorescent wall that glows where exposed and fades over time. Try equations, constellations, wave patterns, drawings, or create temporary silhouettes by blocking the UV.
rules: Use only the UV lights and materials provided. UV lights only on the Glow Wall, never toward another participant's face or eyes. Designs must be appropriate for a college event.

name: Natural Disaster Resilience Track
description: National-level engineering design challenge: teams work on a problem for a month, then present and demonstrate at the fest. Five problem statements (teams may enter any two): PS-01 Flood Vault, PS-02 Ground Zero (earthquake FEM), PS-03 Survivor Seeker (search-and-rescue rover), PS-04 EvacSim (cyclone evacuation planning tool), PS-05 Student Innovation Challenge. Prizes: ₹7,000 for 1st and ₹3,500 for 2nd.
rules: Up to two problem statements per team, each judged independently. Per challenge: Design Report (max 5 pages), Engineering Development Log (Excel), and CAD files with assembly drawing (PS-04: source code and simulation model). 3-minute technical presentation before testing. Single live round: PS-01 is a 10-minute submersion test, PS-03 a timed obstacle course, PS-02/04/05 judged on analysis and presentation.

name: Shark Tank 3.0 (NITW Edition)
description: Innovation-driven competition: pick a real-world problem (science, technology, healthcare, sustainability, engineering, education), research it, and build a working functional prototype. Shortlisted teams pitch before a jury judged on innovation, technical execution, problem-solving, functionality, practicality, and presentation.
rules: Registration, problem statement selection, research and analysis, solution design, working prototype development, final presentation and demo, jury evaluation and Q&A, results and prize distribution.

name: Deconstruct AI
description: Three-round AI challenge combining prompt engineering, reverse engineering, mathematical logic, and research implementation. Round 1 Prompt to Pixel, Round 2 The Black Box Challenge, Round 3 Research to Reality.
rules: Round 1: recreate a complex reference image with AI image generation in a fixed number of attempts; closest matches qualify. Round 2: solve five input-output black-box problems of increasing difficulty; ties broken by time. Round 3: implement a research paper's solution or proof of concept using AI/ML. Final evaluation on implementation, understanding, accuracy, innovation, and presentation.

name: AI Unveiled
description: A collection of interactive AI/ML challenges covering Computer Vision, Deep Learning, NLP, LLMs, RAG, prompt engineering and agent orchestration: Motion Rush (full-body gaming with MediaPipe), Clash of Minds (AI-judged debate), LLM Jailbreak, LLM Orchestration (3-person multi-agent pipeline) and Chromatic Action Matching. Live leaderboards per challenge plus a normalized overall leaderboard; goodies for challenge winners and the top 3 overall.
rules: Register before the event and follow each challenge's instructions. Each game has its own scoring; scores are normalized for the overall leaderboard. LLM Orchestration is a team of 3, all others are individual (Clash of Minds is 1v1). Any attempt to manipulate the software, backend, model, leaderboard or infrastructure leads to disqualification. Ties are broken by completion time or a tie-breaker round. Organizers' decision is final.

name: CSES Arcade
description: Two-day event with a games showcase and a reinforcement learning hackathon. After playing games on multiple stations (including two built by CSES), teams get the game source code at 6 PM and train an RL model to beat it. Work is online until 9 AM on Day 2, then in person, ending with evening presentations.
rules: 3 rounds: Games Showcase, RL Hackathon, Final Evaluation. Models are evaluated mainly on win rate under standardized testing conditions. Final models must be submitted before evaluation; any attempt to manipulate evaluation leads to disqualification.

name: Technozion Data Science Hackathon
description: Two-level data science hackathon supported by Siemens. Teams build data-driven, intelligent applications on Rapidminer AI Studio using data analysis, predictive modelling and intelligent decision-making. Level 1 is online; top teams are shortlisted for the offline finals at NIT Warangal, where they tackle a new problem statement and/or enhance their Level 1 solution. Open to students of any institution and year. Prize pool: ₹25,000 (merchandise).
rules: Teams of 1-3; all members need valid student email IDs. Level 1 (online, Oct 12-24, 2026): solve the released problem statement in Rapidminer AI Studio and submit a zip (College_Abbreviation_TeamName.zip) with the .rmp session file, presentation, 5-15 min video demo (YouTube link) and dataset. Level 2 (offline finals, Oct 30-31, 2026, NIT Warangal): shortlisted teams bring their own laptops and work on a new problem and/or enhance their Level 1 solution; same submission package, no video. Evaluated on model performance, depth of tool exploration and presentation.
